title: Meeting Rooms
description: You are given a list of meeting `Interval` objects, each with a `start` and `end` time. Return `true` if one person could attend every meeting, meaning no two meetings overlap. A meeting that ends at time `t` does not conflict with one that starts at `t`.
hints: If you could line the meetings up in time order, which pairs would you need to compare?
After sorting by start, only neighbouring meetings can conflict.
Return false as soon as a meeting starts before the previous one ends.

solution.explanation: Sort the meetings by start time. If any meeting starts before the previous meeting ends, two meetings overlap and the answer is false. Equal end and start is allowed, so use a strict comparison. Sorting makes it O(n log n) time, and O(1) extra space apart from the sort.
